subject: OrchidHealth - access orchestration & onboarding kickoff
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orchidhealth.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: kickoff: OrchidHealth + Redwood access orchestration

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the intro — excited to get this moving. Attached is our current SSO requirements doc (PDFA) and a short inventory of the identity sources we rely on. High-level goals from our side:

- SSO (SAML) with standard NameID + email, support for persistent SSO sessions
- SCIM for groups + user provisioning (automated deprovisioning required)
- IP allowlist for service-to-service calls from our private subnets
- Dedicated service account(s) for API ingestion, and a policy for rotating keys/credentials

Questions up front: do you have a preferred attribute mapping template? Also — we have a strict retention policy and need to confirm if Redwood will accept a customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.

Samira
Director, IT Security
Orchid Health Systems

Attachments: orchid_sso_requirements_v1.pdf
From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orchidhealth.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@orchidhealth.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff: OrchidHealth + Redwood access orchestration

Hi Samira — thanks for the doc, that’s perfect context. Looping in Monica (Implementation lead) and Laura (Customer Success) who will own the runbook and escalation path.

Quick run-through of next steps from Redwood:

1) Kickoff workshop (30–45m) to align on SAML IdP settings, SCIM attributes, and service-account semantics
2) Share a proposed mapping + scoping spreadsheet (I’ll attach our onboarding matrix)
3) Provide temporary test endpoints and a service-account naming recommendation for Orchid to approve
4) Confirm IP ranges for allowlisting and whether we should target a dedicated VPC connector or shared egress

Can we schedule the workshop Wed 9/9 or Thu 9/10 (PST) morning? I’ll prepare a short checklist for what we need to collect before the session.

Thanks — looking forward to coordinating.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_matrix_v2.xlsx
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff: OrchidHealth + Redwood access orchestration

Samira — quick confirmation from our side: Wed 9/9 at 10:00 AM PST works for us. Agenda I’ll run through (20–30m):

- SAML: required/optional attributes, NameID format, and session lifetime expectations
- SCIM: user <-> group sync cadence, attribute diffs we persist, and how we map Orchid groups to Redwood roles
- Service accounts: naming convention, least-privilege scopes, and rotation cadence
- Network controls: IP allowlist approach and options for VPC connectors
- Compliance: KMS options for Private deployments and audit log availability

Action items for your team before the meeting (please attach to the Drive link if possible):
- IdP metadata (XML) or Okta/Azure screenshot exported
- List of groups to sync and any AD/LDAP filters in place
- IP ranges for allowlisting + contact for network engineer

See you Wednesday — I’ll send a calendar invite with dial-in.

—Laura
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orchidhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: CloudOps <cloudops@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 15:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff: OrchidHealth + Redwood access orchestration

Thanks Laura — confirmed for 9/9 10am PST. A couple of clarifications from engineering:

- For SCIM, we would prefer group membership only (no attribute-overwrite), and a daily sync is fine to start.
- Service-account naming: we’d like something predictable that includes environment and team (e.g., rdw-orchid-prod-sync). Can Redwood provide a short list of recommended scopes we should request?
- On KMS: we can use a customer-managed KMS in our VPC for encryption-at-rest for Private, but for Hosted we’ll need to understand if Redwood can support a Bring-Your-Own-KMS flow or if we need to run Private.

I’ve attached our network range snippet to the Drive link.

—Rajiv
Head of Platform Engineering
Orchid Health Systems
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@orchidhealth.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@orchidhealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: kickoff: OrchidHealth + Redwood access orchestration

Thanks everyone — great kickoff today. Follow-ups and deliverables from Redwood: 

1) I uploaded a starter attribute-mapping CSV to the Drive link (column definitions and suggested defaults). Please review and flag any Orchid-specific attributes by EOD Friday.
2) Service-account guidance: we recommend the naming pattern rdw-orchid-{env}-{purpose} and we suggest two scoped tokens: 
   - rdw-orchid-prod-sync: SCIM write + read, limited to /scim/v2/* endpoints
   - rdw-orchid-monitoring: read-only, embeddings/usage endpoints for telemetry ingestion
   (I attached proposed_service-account-naming.txt for quick copy/paste)
3) IP allowlist: confirmed we can accept the ranges Rajiv linked; we will apply to the hosted egress pool and provide test IPs for validation in 48 hours.
4) KMS: short answer — Hosted does not currently accept customer-managed KMS. If you require BYO-KMS, Private is the recommended path; I included the KMS FAQ link in the Drive.

I'll open a private ticket for the SCIM attribute exceptions that Samira called out so we can track any mapping edge cases. If there's anything urgent, feel free to loop Rishi for SLA exceptions.

Next checkpoint: attribute sign-off and a test SAML assertion by 9/21.

Best,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_service-account-naming.txt
